dossier_meta.statement_text: Is it true that for any finite family of graphs $\mathcal{F}$ that contains at least one forest, there exists a constant $k_0 = k_0(\mathcal{F})$ such that $\mathcal{F}$ is $k$-nice for all $k \geq k_0$?
dossier_meta.context_text: It is easy to see that if $\mathcal{F}$ contains no forest then it is not $k$-nice for any $k$. The question asks whether a converse holds: every family containing at least one forest is eventually $k$-nice. The paper proves this for all families containing a graph with at most 2 edges and for several two-graph families of 3-edge connected graphs.
